title: A2-10 · The suffixed pronouns on verbs and prepositions

blocks.text: A2-10 · The suffixed pronouns on verbs and prepositions
Lesson overview

"I call you tomorrow," "I have seen it" , "dammelo" , "ammelo" said to me: "in Arabic the pronoun complement is not a separate word, but a suffix attached to the verb" ( ⁧رَأَيْتُهُ⁩ I have seen it, or at the preposition ( ⁧قَالَ لِي⁩ He told me. The suffixes you know from the names (A1-09); Here you use them systematically on verbs, with the small shape changes they require, and complete the preposition table. The context is that of phone calls and messages between colleagues: asking for a favor, offering help, leaving a message. A week.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-10), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. attach pronouns to verbs to the perfect, imperfect and imperative, with "mi" = ⁧ـنِي⁩ ;
2. apply shape changes: -tum + suffix → -tumū-, loss of breath, support;
3. use all prepositions with suffixes, including ⁧إِلَيَّ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيَّ⁩ , ⁧فِيَّ⁩ , ⁧لَدَيَّ⁩ ;
4. recognise ⁧إِيَّا⁩ with the second complement ( ⁧أَعْطَانِي إِيَّاهُ⁩ );
5. phone calls, answer the phone, leave and understand a message; ask and offer a favor.

2. The supplementary pronouns on verbs
The suffixes are those of the names (A1-09), with only one difference: ⁧ـنِي⁩ ( -nī), no ⁧ـِي⁩ .
vi / li (dual) ⁧ـهُمَا⁩ · ⁧ـكُمَا⁩ ⁧سَاعَدَهُمَا⁩ · ⁧سَاعَدَكُمَا⁩ ⁧يُسَاعِدُهُمَا⁩ · ⁧يُسَاعِدُكُمَا⁩

The things in the plural are "lei": ⁧الكُتُبُ⁩ … ⁧قَرَأْتُهَا⁩ I read the books...A2-08). The suffix does not change the verb , which maintains its desinence: ⁧سَاعَدَهُ⁩ ( sāʿada-hu), ⁧يُسَاعِدُهُ⁩ ( yusāʿidu-hu), ⁧أَنْ يُسَاعِدَهُ⁩ (subjunctive), ⁧لَمْ يُسَاعِدْهُ⁩ (Giussive). In pause reading the suffix remains whole: yusāʿiduhu, yusāʿid. ⁧ـهُ⁩ becomes ⁧ـهِ⁩ after i, ī, ay, as on names (A1-09) and with prepositions ( ⁧بِهِ⁩ , ⁧فِيهِ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ Section 4): ⁧يُعْطِيهِ⁩ yuʿṭīhi "Gives it', ⁧رَأَيْتِهِ⁩ raʾaytihi You have seen it (you, f.) ⁧اُكْتُبِيهِ⁩ uktubīhi Write it to a woman. Without vowels the difference is not seen: ⁧يعطيه⁩ , ⁧رأيته⁩ .

blocks.text: ⁧رَآهُ.⁩ ⁧رَأَى⁩ + ⁧هُ⁩ It is written with the Madda: ⁧رَآهُ⁩ raʾāhu He saw it. ⁧رَأَتْهُ⁩ You have seen it/you have seen it. The verb "I" to the perfect ends in -you: ⁧رَأَيْتُهُ⁩ I've seen it. ⁧سَاعَدْتُكَ⁩ I helped you. Do not confuse with ?tu (m.) ⁧رَأَيْتَهُ⁩ You have seen it, without vowels you write equal ( ⁧رأيته⁩ ).
4. The prepositions with the suffixes
You know many; Here is the complete table of the most frequent prepositions. Attention to columns with special shapes.

⁧مِنْ⁩ Of a thickness of not more than 1 mm

blocks.text: Three rules explain the special forms:
1. ⁧إِلَى⁩ , ⁧عَلَى⁩ , ⁧لَدَى⁩ (which end up in -ā written ⁧ى⁩ ) become -ay- in front of the suffix: ⁧إِلَيْكَ⁩ , ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ ; with icing
diphthong merges with the ī: ⁧إِلَيَّ⁩ Ilayya, ⁧عَلَيَّ⁩ ʿalayya, ⁧لَدَيَّ⁩ Ladayya.
2. ⁧فِي⁩ With a "-io--' ⁧فِيَّ⁩ Fiyya.
3. ⁧مِنْ⁩ , ⁧عَنْ⁩ double the ⁧ن⁩ before -ī and -nā: ⁧مِنِّي⁩ , ⁧عَنِّي⁩ , ⁧مِنَّا⁩ , ⁧عَنَّا⁩ .

⁧لَدَى⁩ means press, as ⁧عِنْدَ⁩ , but it is more formal: it is frequent in administrative and journalistic texts to have , ( ⁧لَدَيْهِ مَعْلُومَاتٌ⁩ • has information (s) and for press (s) ⁧السَّفِيرُ لَدَى الأُمَمِ المُتَّحِدَةِ⁩ The Ambassador to the United Nations. Verbs with preposition. Many verbs hold a preposition, and the pronoun attaches itself to that: ⁧أَتَّصِلُ بِكَ⁩ I'm calling you. ⁧أَبْحَثُ عَنْهُ⁩ I'm looking for him. ⁧سَأَلَ عَنْكِ⁩ He asked for you, ⁧قُلْتُ لَهَا⁩ I told her, ⁧أَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْكُمْ⁩ I need you. ⁧سَمَحَ لِي⁩ "It allowed me to do so," ⁧رَدَّ عَلَيْنَا⁩ He replied to us. Always learn the verb with his preposition: in English he often does not exist.
5. Two complements: ⁧إِيَّا⁩
Some verbs have two direct complements: ⁧أَعْطَى⁩ • give and ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ • ask for • ⁧سَأَلْتُهُ سُؤَالًا⁩ I asked him a question.

two pronouns ⁧أَعْطَيْتُهُ إِيَّاهُ.⁩ I gave it to him. When the second complement is also a pronoun, it does not stick to the verb but to ⁧إِيَّا⁩ + suffix: ⁧إِيَّاهُ⁩ , ⁧إِيَّاهَا⁩ , ⁧إِيَّاهُمْ⁩ . It is a construction to be recognized: in the current use you often prefer to repeat the name ( ⁧أَعْطَيْتُهُ⁩
⁧المِفْتَاحَ⁩ ).
⁧إِيَّا⁩ it also appears in fixed expressions: ⁧إِيَّاكَ أَنْ⁩ ... woe to thee if... ⁧إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ⁩ We adore you in the first sura of the Qur'an).

Culture. A telephone call or a work message between Arabic colleagues almost always begins with a greeting and a question about health before the actual request; To enter into the substance immediately may seem abrupt. On the contrary, in written service messages (A2-22) the formal register has its own formulas.
7. Pronunciation

-nī, -ka, -hu. The suffixes are part of the word: the accent moves towards the end. yu-sā-ʿi-du-nī, sa-ʾa-la-nī, ra- ʾay-tu-hu. fiyya, layya, ʿalayya. The y is double: fiy-ya, ʿa-lay-ya. A simple y changes shape (ʿalayā There is no such thing. minnī, ʿannī. The double n feels: min-nī. Don't say ""minī». raʾāhu. raʾā + hu: la ā stays long in front of the suffix, ra-ʾā-hu.
